dimensions.assessment: Affects sponsors of drug and biological product applications, holders of approved applications, and patent owners.
dimensions.evidence: requires applicants seeking approval of a drug or licensure of a biological product to submit certain information

dimensions.assessment: Imposes new certification duties and creates a non-disclosure defense against patent infringement actions.
dimensions.evidence: A person shall be entitled to a defense under section 282(b) in an action asserting infringement of an applicable patent

dimensions.assessment: The source material does not state specific federal spending or revenue numbers.
Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, the Public Health Service Act, and Title 35 of the United States Code.
dimensions.evidence: Section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. 355(b)) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Applies permanently to original applications submitted on or after enactment and to specified future submissions and patents for prior applications.
dimensions.evidence: apply with respect to any original application submitted under this subsection on or after the date of enactment

missing_information: Specific estimates of federal administrative costs or savings
importance_detail.rationale: The bill establishes new disclosure and certification requirements for drug and biological product applications submitted to the FDA and USPTO, creating a specific legal defense in patent infringement actions for non-disclosure. It directly affects drug and biological product application sponsors, patent holders, and federal agencies.
